learning_objectives: Understand and use four-way vowel harmony.
scope_included: choose ı, i, u or ü in transparent practice forms, using -(I)m only as a declared carrier for form recognition
scope_excluded: possession syntax, consonant alternations and lexical exceptions

references.title: Türk Dil Kurumu: 2026 Yazım Kılavuzu – Sesler ve Ses Uyumları
Karadeniz Teknik Üniversitesi, Türk Dili Bölümü: Güz Dönemi Ders İçerikleri – Türkçenin Ses Bilgisi ve İyelik Ekleri

skills.description_en: Recognise the narrow vowel ı/i/u/ü in a four-way harmony practice form.
Identify the final vowel of an A1 noun and use both back/front and rounded/unrounded information.
Choose the correct vowel in the declared -(I)m practice carrier for a regular consonant-final noun.
Write a complete regular noun form with ım/im/um/üm according to the final stem vowel.

lesson.short_explanation_en: The earlier lesson chose between a and e. Now a four-way pattern chooses between ı, i, u and ü. Look at the last vowel of a word: a or ı selects ı; e or i selects i; o or u selects u; ö or ü selects ü. We practise this in regular consonant-ending noun forms with the ending -(I)m: balım, evim, yolum, gözüm. These forms can be translated as “my honey”, “my home”, “my road” and “my eye”, but this micro-lesson focuses on the written vowel, not on possession syntax.

rule_blocks.heading_en: Four choices from the final vowel
rule_blocks.explanation_en: Four-way vowel harmony selects one of four narrow vowels: ı, i, u or ü. The last stem vowel determines the choice: a/ı → ı; e/i → i; o/u → u; ö/ü → ü. First find the final vowel, then match both its back/front quality and its rounded/unrounded quality.
rule_blocks.pattern: a, ı → ı | e, i → i | o, u → u | ö, ü → ü
usage_notes_en: This is a four-way choice, unlike the earlier two-way a/e harmony.
For this lesson, the narrow vowel appears only in the declared -(I)m pattern.
We use consonant-ending words without consonant changes or vowel loss; ownership grammar and complete possessive constructions are taught later.
common_errors_en: balim is incorrect for this practice form: after a, choose dotless ı, giving balım.
gözum is incorrect: ö selects ü, so write gözüm.

rule_blocks.heading_en: Keep the stem and attach the practice ending
rule_blocks.explanation_en: Here -(I)m is a declared carrier for seeing the ı/i/u/ü distinction. For a regular consonant-final noun, attach the chosen vowel plus m with no space: ev → evim and okul → okulum. These forms can be glossed “my …”, but the lesson tests only vowel choice, not possessive syntax.
rule_blocks.pattern: consonant-final noun + -(I)m → balım / evim / yolum / gözüm
usage_notes_en: Write the complete form as one word.
The I in -(I)m is a pattern label, never a literal capital I in the written word.
Avoid vowel-final nouns, changes to the noun stem, and exceptions in this lesson.
common_errors_en: kalemım is not the form: the last vowel e requires i, making kalemim.
üzümim uses the wrong vowel: final ü requires ü, giving üzümüm.

contexts.setting_en: In a Turkish classroom, Ayşe and Mehmet compare their written word labels and isolate the narrow vowel in each ending.

lines.speaker: Mehmet
lines.translation_en: “Kalemim” and “defterim” both have i in the ending.

lines.speaker: Ayşe
lines.translation_en: “Okulum” uses u in the ending, while “sınıfım” uses ı.

contexts.setting_en: In a shared kitchen, Zeynep writes short ownership labels on food containers and checks the vowels.

lines.speaker: Zeynep
lines.translation_en: My milk, my honey and my salt.

lines.speaker: Zeynep
lines.target: Sütüm: ü. Balım: ı. Tuzum: u.
lines.translation_en: The added vowels are ü in “sütüm”, ı in “balım” and u in “tuzum”.

examples.note_en: The final a is back and unrounded: choose ı.
The final dotless ı selects ı.
The final o is back and rounded: choose u.
The final e is front and unrounded: choose i.
The final ö is front and rounded: choose ü.
The last vowel is e, so the written form uses im.
The last vowel is ü, so add üm: üzümüm.

exercises.instruction_en: Choose the correct option.
exercises.prompt_en: Which vowel is inserted immediately before m in balım?

options.explanation_en: Final a selects dotless ı.
i is front and cannot match a.
u would match o or u.
ü would match ö or ü.

hint_steps: Locate the added vowel before m.
Final stem vowel a is back and unrounded.
exercises.feedback_correct_en: Correct. You matched the final stem vowel to the four-way ending.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: balım contains dotless ı before m, not i, u or ü.
exercises.explanation_en: a → ı in this four-way ending.

exercises.instruction_en: Choose the correct option.
exercises.prompt_en: Which vowel is inserted immediately before m in evim?

options.explanation_en: ı goes with a or ı.
Final e selects i.
u goes with o or u.
ü goes with ö or ü.

hint_steps: Look immediately before final m.
Final stem vowel e is front and unrounded.
exercises.feedback_correct_en: Correct. You matched the final stem vowel to the four-way ending.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: evim has i before m; the form evım would be wrong.
exercises.explanation_en: e → i in this four-way ending.

exercises.instruction_en: Choose the correct option.
exercises.prompt_en: Which vowel is inserted immediately before m in yolum?

options.explanation_en: ı matches a or ı.
ü matches ö or ü.
Final o selects u.
i matches e or i.

hint_steps: Look at the final stem vowel, not the first consonant.
The rounded back vowel o selects u.
exercises.feedback_correct_en: Correct. You matched the final stem vowel to the four-way ending.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: yolum has u; yolım would ignore rounding.
exercises.explanation_en: o → u in this four-way ending.

exercises.instruction_en: Choose the correct option.
exercises.prompt_en: Which vowel is inserted immediately before m in gözüm?

options.explanation_en: u is the rounded back choice.
i is the unrounded front choice.
ı is unrounded and back.
Final ö selects ü.

hint_steps: Compare ö with the four groups.
Rounded front ö pairs with ü.
exercises.feedback_correct_en: Correct. You matched the final stem vowel to the four-way ending.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: The ending in gözüm contains ü, not u.
exercises.explanation_en: ö → ü in this four-way ending.

vocabulary_audit.note: All annotations use reviewed A1 dictionary headwords. The bound endings -ım/-im/-um/-üm are grammar, not vocabulary entries. Isolated vowels and isolated letter names are not counted as lemmas.

level_audit.note: A1 writing and recognition: four-way vowel choice only, using -(I)m as a declared form carrier. All graded stems end in a consonant; no alternations, exceptions or possessive syntax are taught. The prerequisite topics were delivered in previous turns.
